description: A research question: a scientific unknown that we want to make known, addressable by the systematic application of research methods. Questions organize inquiry; claims address them (see tech.scios.rrgi.addresses). Grounded in the MIRA community schema (github.com/MIRA-science/schema, mira.yaml, Question class); first ported (2026-05) from the DiscourseGraphs coalition's OWL (github.com/DiscourseGraphs/schemas, dg:Question) — historical lineage, kept as attribution. Dual-addressing of every reference is an RRGI extension intended to be proposed upstream.

text.description: The research question: a scientific unknown posed for systematic investigation.

description.description: Optional elaboration: scope, motivation, or context for the question.

contextEntities.description: Aboutness: the concrete concepts and entities this question is about (e.g. phenomena, materials, instruments, datasets, populations, tasks) — the same field claims and evidence carry. Records point at external subject authorities rather than minting an internal entity registry, following Wikidata P921 'main subject' ('primary topic of a work or act of communication') and schema.org 'about' ('The subject matter of an object'); each entry's optional uri resolves to the external authority. Stamped at authoring/decomposition time; enables shared-concept joins across literatures — an open question and a distant claim about one concept become findable together.

name.description: Name or identifier of the concept or entity. Prefer specific over generic — a rare, precise concept is worth more to discovery than a broad one.

uri.description: Optional URI identifying this entity in an external ontology or knowledge base (e.g. a Wikidata item) — the P921/about pattern: reference external authorities, never mint an internal registry.
